subject.title: docs(durable): rebuild 2026.7.1 beta 3 durable core RFC and proof plan

question: Should this release/2026.7.1 architecture and test plan replace the overlapping main-targeted RFC as the canonical durable-core document, and do current state/task/runtime owners approve its cross-owner boundary?
rationale: Both proposals are technically plausible and the patch has no remaining mechanical defect; selecting the public source, target branch, and permanent ownership model requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Consolidate on current main
options.body: Keep one main-based RFC and fold in this PR's improved existing-store description and proof-plan material after explicit owner review.

options.title: Adopt the release rebuild
options.body: Publish this split Beta 3 RFC and test plan, then reconcile or close the older main-targeted proposal.

options.title: Pause both proposals
options.body: Defer public umbrella architecture until the implementation sequence and cross-owner boundary are approved.

recommendation.title: Consolidate on current main
recommendation.body: Keep one main-based RFC and fold in this PR's improved existing-store description and proof-plan material after explicit owner review.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent database-first and SQLite task architecture is the strongest direct provenance for the proposed shared durable boundary.
